claims.text: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits negligible irradiation-induced hardening and robust radiation resistance.
Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops Cr/V-rich precipitates at approximately 8 dpa.
Adding 1–2 at% Hf will suppress irradiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitate formation in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The Hf-modified alloy will retain low irradiation-induced hardening and high radiation resistance.
Mechanical alloying and powder consolidation provide a practical route for introducing 1–2 at% Hf into the alloy.
The proposed behavior applies through 8 dpa at specimen temperatures below approximately 800°C.
Keeping the specimen below approximately 800°C will limit thermal diffusion and preserve the nanocrystalline structure.
Hf atoms will preferentially segregate to grain boundaries and irradiation-induced defect sinks.
Segregated Hf will trap Cr and V atoms at internal interfaces and defect clusters.
Trapping of Cr and V by Hf will reduce Cr and V mobility.
Reduced Cr and V mobility will hinder nucleation and growth of Cr/V-rich precipitates.
Suppression of precipitation will stabilize the favorable nanocrystalline microstructure.
Microstructural stabilization will preserve resistance to radiation-induced hardening.
After 8 dpa, the Hf-modified alloy will have a statistically significant reduction in Cr/V-rich precipitate density relative to the unmodified alloy.
After 8 dpa, the Hf-modified alloy will have smaller Cr/V-rich precipitates than the unmodified alloy.
After irradiation, the Hf-modified alloy will exhibit a finer defect morphology and no increase in hardening relative to the control.
Cr/V-rich precipitates in unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 increase hardening and brittleness at approximately 8 dpa.
Variations in Hf concentration or chemical homogeneity could produce unintended Hf-rich phases.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field says the alloy shows negligible hardening despite precipitate formation near 8 dpa, whereas the baseline says those precipitates increase hardening and brittleness at approximately the same dose.
